learning_objective: 🎯 Master the art of inviting people! Learn the differences between formal card-style invitations, official letters, and casual informal ones.

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: कृपया उत्तर दें (Répondez s'il vous plaît)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Used for weddings, school functions, or big events. They are written in the third person (He/She/They/Names). No signatures are used. RSVP is written at the bottom left.
Used to invite a VIP or Chief Guest. It follows the standard formal letter format (Sender's Add, Date, Receiver's Add, Subject, Salutation, Body, Closing).
Used for friends and close relatives (birthdays, small parties). Written in the first person ('I', 'We'). The tone is warm, relaxed, and personal. Follows informal letter format.
Always thank the host. Confirm your presence. In formal replies, use third person ('Mr. Sharma thanks Mr. Verma for the invitation and is delighted to accept...').
Politely thank them, state a valid reason for your absence (e.g., prior engagement/health issues), and send good wishes for the event.

fun_activity.title: 💌 The RSVP Challenge
fun_activity.instructions: Draft a 2-line formal refusal to a wedding invitation because you have a board exam the next day. Remember, use the Third Person! (e.g., 'Rohan regrets his inability to attend...')

exam_tips: 📌 Card-style formal invitations must be enclosed in a BOX.
📌 Never use abbreviations (like 'don't' or 'can't') in formal invitations.
📌 Always include Date, Time, and Venue clearly in every invitation.
quick_recap: ⭐ Card invitations: 3rd person. Letter invitations: 1st/2nd person.
⭐ RSVP is a French phrase asking the guest to confirm if they are coming.
⭐ Replies are just as important as the invitation—keep them short (50 words).
